cd "/mnt/c/Users/Jerome Hollon/Documents/claude/astrophotography-explainer" && mkdir -p assets/thanks && uv run python - <<'EOF'
from PIL import Image, ImageOps
import glob, os
srcs = sorted(glob.glob('source_images/thanks/*.jpg'))
for i, f in enumerate(srcs, 1):
    im = ImageOps.exif_transpose(Image.open(f)).convert('RGB')
    im.thumbnail((1600, 1600), Image.LANCZOS)
    out = f'assets/thanks/observatory_{i}.jpg'
    im.save(out, 'JPEG', quality=85, optimize=True, progressive=True)
    print(out, im.size, os.path.getsize(out)//1024, 'KB', '<-', os.path.basename(f))
EOF
cat > tools/assets/thanks_photos.py <<'EOF'
"""Web-sized copies of the observatory photos shown in the thank-you modal.

    uv run tools/assets/thanks_photos.py

Reads source_images/thanks/*.jpg (git-ignored originals), applies the EXIF
orientation, fits each inside 1600 px and writes assets/thanks/observatory_<n>.jpg.
"""
import glob, os
from PIL import Image, ImageOps

os.makedirs('assets/thanks', exist_ok=True)
for i, f in enumerate(sorted(glob.glob('source_images/thanks/*.jpg')), 1):
    im = ImageOps.exif_transpose(Image.open(f)).convert('RGB')
    im.thumbnail((1600, 1600), Image.LANCZOS)
    out = f'assets/thanks/observatory_{i}.jpg'
    im.save(out, 'JPEG', quality=85, optimize=True, progressive=True)
    print(out, im.size)
EOF

## 1. "Average results in a lot of hot pixels" — the pipeline is correct; the specks are physical

Method: ran the actual TS pipeline (stackWith + inlineExecutor) in node straight off data/derived/runtime bin-2 files for the galaxy ROI (ref f03, bin 2, 720×480, dark|flat_50_darkflat, 20 raw frames) and the trail ROI, and compared with a numpy Lanczos-3 reference (tools/golden/reference.py) on the same files.

  • TS average vs numpy: NaN masks identical, median |d| = 0.000 DN, p99 = 0.000, max 2.0 DN (one star core). TS median vs numpy: median 0.000, max 8 DN (star core). Single East frame f10 warped vs numpy: max 0.001 DN, so East frames get the dark, the 180° handling and the per-pier-side master union right. NaN handling: nanmean-equivalent (a NaN in one frame does not poison the pixel). Reference frame f03 is the identity warp as expected. Normalization matches.
  • Review-page PNG (numpy cubic spline, stack_galaxy_average.png) shows the same specks: 3552 pixels >5σ above local background vs 4218 for the TS average under the same stretch (Lanczos is sharper), pixel diff median 2.8/255.

Why the average shows specks (numbers at the 1946 hot pixels the master dark flags in the galaxy ROI, excess over a 7×7 local median, bin-2 DN): - master dark removes only 34 % of the hot-pixel excess (design-notes §5 item 11 says 37 %). - single frame f03: p50 excess 75 DN, σ 20.0, 705 of 1946 above 5σ. - 20-frame average: p50 9.0 DN, σ 4.4, 334 above 5σ (ratio avg/single ≈ 0.36 at f03's own positions). - 20-frame median: p50 3.7 DN, σ 5.0, 11 above 5σ (clean). - Speck census (all >5σ pixels incl. stars, 720×480): single 1678, average 6211, median 2721. The reason the average keeps ~1/10 rather than 1/20: the frames were dithered in PAIRS, not 20 distinct positions. Offsets of the ROI centre relative to f03 (native px): f00 (1.0,1.3), f01 (1.8,1.1), f02 (0.6,−0.3), f03 (0,0); f04/f05 (33.3,35.0)/(33.7,35.4); f06/f07 (27.0,26.3)/(27.7,26.6); f08/f09 (−214.7,−7.4)/(−215.8,−7.0); f10/f11 (−217.6,−16.8)/(−217.6,−17.0); … f18/f19 (−222.2,18.4)/(−222.1,18.9). So each hot pixel lands on the same bin-2 output pixel from 2 frames (4 for the f00–f03 cluster): 2–4/20 of a 75 DN excess ≈ 8–15 DN vs 4.4 DN stack noise = visible speck. The median sees 2–4 hot samples of 20 and ignores them. No cosmetic correction is applied (SPEC §6.7). Owner's decision: enable a cosmetic-correction option (or leave as a teaching point: average vs median on hot pixels).

Test: src/shared/pipeline/hotpixels.test.ts + fixtures/hotpixels.json (868 KB; 20 real frames, 56×56 bin-2 window at native (3822,2228), 28 dark-flagged hot pixels, per-pier-side master crops). Generated by the new section (f) in tools/golden/make_fixtures.py: uv run tools/golden/make_fixtures.py --only hotpixels (reads only data/derived/runtime, no source_images). Asserts average/median/reference-frame pixel agreement with numpy (median <0.002 DN, max <0.5) and the residual physics (avg keeps between 1/20 and 4/20 of the single-frame excess and stays above σ; median residual below σ, 0 above 5σ).

## 2. Autocrop export API (for the workbench agent)

All exported from src/shared/pipeline (index.ts):

ts commonCrop(req: StackRequest, frames: Manifest | Pick<Sources,'frame'>): Rect | null // largest axis-aligned rect every frame of req contributes to, in RESULT samples (x,y from 0, w<=result.w, h<=result.h); null if none commonCropLive(req: StackRequest): Promise<Rect | null> // same, resolving frames from the live manifest cropResult(result: StackResult, rect: Rect): StackResult // copy cut to rect (noise, ms kept) exportPng(result, stf, { rotate180?: boolean; crop?: Rect | null }): Promise<Blob> // crop applied before rotation exportFits(result, header, { crop?: Rect | null }): Blob Typical wiring: const crop = await commonCropLive(req); const blob = await exportPng(result, stf, { rotate180, crop }); (fitsHeaderFor(req, result) unchanged; pass the same crop to exportFits). Omit crop for the uncropped export. The UI can draw the cropped extent from the same rect (result-sample coordinates; multiply by grid.bin for native). Also exported: validOutputRect, intersectRect (geometry.ts).

Implementation: geometric (each frame's closed sensor rect mapped back through M⁻¹, inscribed axis-aligned rect, corner samples re-verified by the warp's own forward test), intersected over frames and the output rect. No change to StackResult or the worker protocol. Verified on real data: 20 frames, whole reference frame at bin 8, West (f03) and East (f10) references: 0 NaN samples inside the crop for every frame; crop {x:11,y:9,w:762,h:507} of 778×521 for ref f03. Unit tests in src/shared/pipeline/crop.test.ts (two synthetic frames offset by (5,−3), East flip at bin 1 and 2, real-like homography, Manifest input, cropped FITS NAXIS/row order).
